children: received a higher target from Truist as the firm sees growing cybersecurity needs tied to artificial intelligence supporting broader use of the company's platform.

Truist kept a Buy rating on the shares while raising its price target to $300 from $245. The call comes as CrowdStrike hosts its Fal.Con 2026 conference in Las Vegas, where investors are looking for more detail on future recurring-revenue growth.

Analyst Junaid Siddiqui said the firm will watch for updated expectations around net new annual recurring revenue, longer-term targets and product expansion. He also pointed to the security challenges created by increasingly capable AI systems and autonomous agents.

Those concerns became more visible after Anthropic's Claude Mythos model demonstrated the ability to uncover software vulnerabilities. Truist now expects CrowdStrike could expand its role across areas including identity controls, threat detection, AI governance and protection of agent-based systems.
For CRWD stock, the higher target suggests Truist sees the AI-driven security environment as a potential catalyst for additional growth.

title: 5-Star Analyst Revamps CrowdStrike Price Target for 2027
